name: Unseen Predator

values.label: Landing distance from target's location at dash start, determines dash length

parts.label: Innate
parts.text: Innate: Upon casting a basic ability or using Savagery first attack, Rengar generates a stack of Ferocity for 1 second, stacking up 4 times but not refreshing on subsequent triggers . At maximum stacks, his next basic ability consumes them all to become empowered with an additional effect and grant him an additional cast along with 30 / 40 / 50 (based on level)% bonus movement speed for 1.5 seconds. Generated Ferocity is prevented from expiring for 10 seconds after dealing or taking damage, excluding damage dealt by damage over time or proc effects.

values.context: At maximum stacks, his next basic ability consumes them all to become empowered with an additional effect and grant him an additional cast along with 30 / 40 / 50 (based on level)% bonus movement speed for 1.5 seconds.

tips.tip: counting from the end of attack windup or cast time

parts.label: Innate
parts.text: Innate: While in brush, Rengar gains Unseen Predator, which lingers for 0.35 seconds upon exiting brush. Unseen Predator is lost immediately if Rengar exits the brush using Flash or Hexflash.

mechanics.evidence: Innate: While in brush, Rengar gains Unseen Predator, which lingers for 0.35 seconds upon exiting brush.

parts.label: Unseen Predator
parts.text:
Unseen Predator: Rengar's next basic attack on-attack generates 1 Ferocity if none of his current Ferocity was generated this way. The attack also has massively increased range and causes him to leap to the target's location if they are beyond his normal basic attack range, attacking the target upon arrival and landing 50 units in front of them.

Rengar can cast any of his abilities during the dash. The start of the leap is the end of Rengar's attack windup, putting the attack timer on cooldown, triggering on-attack effects and additionally refreshing the Ferocity duration.

parts.text: Innate - Bonetooth Necklace: Scoring a takedown against an enemy champion within 3 seconds of damaging them grants Rengar a Trophy, once per unique champion and up to 5. An additional Trophy is made available through the event The Hunt is On! with the Head of Kha'Zix. Trophies grant bonus attack damage equal to 1 / 4 / 9 / 16 / 25 / 36 (based on Trophies)% bonus AD.

values.context: Trophies grant bonus attack damage equal to 1 / 4 / 9 / 16 / 25 / 36 (based on Trophies)% bonus AD.

notes:
Rengar has a secondary resource bar that indicates how much Ferocity he currently has as pips.
  - Ferocity generated by Unseen Predator has a purple color.
  - Ferocity generated by his other abilities has a white color.
Only Flash and Hexflash instantly end Unseen Predator. Other blink effects will still cause the buff to linger upon exiting the brush area.
The attack deals basic damage but is considered ability damage for Spear of Shojin.
While grounded or rooted, Rengar loses the enhanced attack range from Unseen Predator.

Rapid Firecannon and Savagery bonus ranges are lost after 0.25 seconds upon gaining Unseen Predator, and are re-gained after 0.25 seconds upon losing Unseen Predator.
  - The same does not apply for other bonus ranges such as Hexoptics C44.
Rengar will only leap to a target if his basic attack timer has been refreshed (if not so he will not automatically attempt to path towards his target, despite them being within leap range).

Rengar can freely use any abilities, summoner spells, or item actives while leaping.
  - Using a dash or blink ability will interrupt the leap.

The attack from the leap will:
  - Not go off if the dash was interrupted.
  - Not go off if the target becomes untargetable.
  - Go off at the end of the dash even if its normal destination is obstructed by boundaries he cannot cross (e.g. terrain, The Hextech Ultimatum).
  - Go off regardless of distance the enemy travels away from Rengar's original location.
  - Go off even if Rengar loses sight of the target.
Bonus AD percent from Bonetooth Necklace stacks recursively with Infernal Might, Overlord's Bloodmail Tyranny and mid lane quest's bonus AD multiplier.

Bonetooth Necklace uses different icons corresponding to the number of stacks acquired:
  - 1 Stack:
  - 2 Stacks:
  - 3 Stacks:
  - 4 Stacks:
  - 5 Stacks:
  - 6th Stack: Head of Kha'Zix

name: Thrill of the Hunt

parts.label: Passive
parts.text: Passive: Rengar also gains Unseen Predator while camouflaged from any source.

mechanics.evidence: Passive: Rengar also gains Unseen Predator while camouflaged from any source.

parts.label: Active
parts.text:
Active: Rengar prowls for a duration, gaining bonus movement speed. After a 2-second delay, he also becomes camouflaged and gains Unseen Predator.

The camouflage can only last up to 14 seconds.

mechanics.evidence: After a 2-second delay, he also becomes camouflaged and gains Unseen Predator.

parts.text: During this time, Rengar will detect the nearest enemy champion in range, revealing and gaining sight of a 100-unit radius around them. Enemies detected are revealed for the remaining full duration.

mechanics.evidence: During this time, Rengar will detect the nearest enemy champion in range, revealing and gaining sight of a 100-unit radius around them.
During this time, Rengar will detect the nearest enemy champion in range, revealing and gaining sight of a 100-unit radius around them.
Enemies detected are revealed for the remaining full duration.

parts.text: The nearest detected enemy within 1600 range is also marked, alerting all of their allies within 1200 range about Rengar's presence.

Rengar's next basic attack within range 125 range against any enemy or with Unseen Predator to the marked enemy deals 100% AD additional physical damage and then inflicts armor reduction for 4 seconds.

The target is revealed until the leap has finished.

mechanics.evidence: The target is revealed until the leap has finished.

parts.text: Attacking or casting abilities other than Savagery ends Thrill of the Hunt immediately.

notes: Thrill of the Hunt's duration starts on-cast.

The ability applies a mark on the target at the start of attack windup that is successively consumed when the basic attack hits to apply the effect.
  - If the attack is prevented or blocked (e.g. by knocking down Rengar when leaping) then the effect will not be applied.
    - The mark will however still linger for a very short period after that, allowing Rengar to consume it with a quick basic attack. [https://github.com/ArdaSenyurek/Rengar-Bugs/issues/108]
The ability deals basic damage.
Rengar discerns a distinct heart beat instead of the usual true sight indicator. This indicator will be removed when out of range, but the target will remain revealed.
Thrill of the Hunt has an indicator that appears above the target(s) when Rengar is nearby. Some skins have a unique indicator.

name: Battle Roar

parts.label: Passive
parts.text: Passive: Rengar stores 50% of the post-mitigation damage he has taken in the last 1.5 seconds as grey health on his health bar, increased to 100% of damage taken from monsters.

parts.label: Active
parts.text: Active: Rengar roars, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies and 65 – 130 (based on level) bonus magic damage to monsters, and consuming his grey health to heal for the same amount.

mechanics.evidence: Active: Rengar roars, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies and 65 – 130 (based on level) bonus magic damage to monsters, and consuming his grey health to heal for the same amount.

values.context: Active: Rengar roars, dealing magic damage to nearby enemies and 65 – 130 (based on level) bonus magic damage to monsters, and consuming his grey health to heal for the same amount.

parts.label: Ferocity Bonus
parts.text: Ferocity Bonus: Battle Roar's damage is modified to deal 50 – 220 (based on level) (+ 80% AP) magic damage. Rengar cleanses himself from all crowd control.

mechanics.evidence: Rengar cleanses himself from all crowd control.

values.context: Ferocity Bonus: Battle Roar's damage is modified to deal 50 – 220 (based on level) (+ 80% AP) magic damage.

notes: Grey health will not be consumed upon casting Battle Roar despite visually appearing so. It will only ever expire after its duration ends.
